findings.reason: the repair as scoped cannot change the state the incident occurred in, and its endpoint, read literally, would break the trust guard §42 landed, so the deliverable has to name what the supervisor should do when the checkout is untrusted and has moved, which is the actual defect the log shows.
findings.text: §51 says §42's comparison "runs only in `reload()`, not on the supervisor's regular check" and that the admit service therefore ran stale for ten hours; the supervisor's log at `~/.local/state/fleet/fleet-1291586.log` shows its own loop detecting the move at 21:56:25Z on 10 November and logging 614 refusals, one per sixty-second tick, reading "the checkout is not trusted (M reckon/_plan_html.py, M reckon/_store.py, M reckon/_store_section_ops.py), so this image and the declared services keep running the code they started on", until trust returned and the service restarted at 08:22:03Z on 11 November — 10 h 42 min, and not the 13:57 respawn the plan names; §42's `_runs_recorded_code` (fleet_supervisor.py:1424) honours the same trust flag, so a comparison added to the regular check either does nothing in the incident state or, if it ignores trust, restarts services onto a checkout the supervisor was deliberately refusing

findings.reason: an arm staging the untrusted, moved checkout (and asserting what the supervisor must then report or do) is the only case that would have failed at the base revision for the reason the incident failed, so without it the node's gate proves nothing about the report's own subject.
findings.text: the gate's reproduction is "a declared service started on one commit, main moved to a commit changing a module that service imports, and after a supervisor check the service still runs the old stamp" on a temporary checkout, and its only negative control restores base behaviour for that comparable case, so no arm puts the moved checkout in the untrusted state that produced the incident and the test reports green on code that leaves the incident untouched

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `~/.local/state/fleet/services/reckon-admit-local.log`, `~/.config/reckon/crew/admission-verdicts.jsonl`, `reload()` in `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, the commit `21ccbe709d` and the tree stamps `dc2eb54`/`dc2eb5471bfe` all resolve (the verdict rows at 07:53Z and 08:13Z have since rotated out of a file that now retains rows only from 15:05Z, which is retention, not a broken pointer).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §51's done-when stages a temporary checkout whose stamp the supervisor can compare, so the state the incident actually had (a moved stamp on an untrusted checkout) is never reached and the gate passes whether or not the incident's cause is touched.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — logs are required under the run directory, opened with the revision and literal command and closed with `EXIT=`, and both arms run on the `all_debug` partition rather than the fleet node.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test name and the section text carry no plan labels or ticket numbers, and the mechanism is stated in code terms.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §51's stated root cause is contradicted by the supervisor's own log, which shows the comparison firing every sixty seconds through the whole window and refusing on the checkout's trust flag, so the ten-hour staleness is the trust gate working as §42 designed it, not a comparison missing from the regular check.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one endpoint, the stamp comparison applied on the supervisor's regular check, with the unreadable-stamp report as the second arm of the same comparison rather than a separate deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s42 is now `descoped` with its unmet half delegated to §51, `plan-section-declarations` and `plan-section-depends-on` carry no contradiction, and the open followup `f-wns-006` names §51, so the chain has a next step.
